builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HybridSpec: Throughput-Aware Speculative Decoding for Hybrid GDN-MoE Models
summary: HybridSpec replaces fixed-length speculative verification in DFlash-style decoding with GPU-side adaptive verification-length selection, early MoE routing correction, and block-parallel GDN kernels with single-launch state reconstruction. It costs custom GDN kernel implementation, draft-side acceptance estimation, on-GPU latency measurement, and added verification-pipeline complexity, and it is tied to hybrid GDN-MoE architectures. It can fail if acceptance estimates are miscalibrated, if router correction rejects useful tokens or admits wasted ones, if kernels are unavailable for the deployment stack, or if the reader's models are dense rather than GDN-MoE.
rationale: The gains are substantial but contingent on running hybrid GDN-MoE target models and on custom kernels and integration work that are not yet a drop-in option for a small team, so adoption should wait for mature serving-stack support.
technique: Throughput-aware adaptive speculative decoding for hybrid GDN-MoE models

claims.statement: HybridSpec replaces fixed-length speculative verification in DFlash-style decoding with GPU-side adaptive verification-length selection, early MoE routing correction, and block-parallel GDN kernels with single-launch state reconstruction. It costs custom GDN kernel implementation, draft-side acceptance estimation, on-GPU latency measurement, and added verification-pipeline complexity, and it is tied to hybrid GDN-MoE architectures. It can fail if acceptance estimates are miscalibrated, if router correction rejects useful tokens or admits wasted ones, if kernels are unavailable for the deployment stack, or if the reader's models are dense rather than GDN-MoE.

Single-request greedy decoding is 1.75x-1.88x faster than autoregressive decoding and 1.30x-1.33x faster than DFlash on three GDN-MoE target models; isolated GDN kernels are 1.54x-4.04x faster than default kernels.
